questions: Does the sensor signal stay monotonic and usable across the full ±0.03 m range, or does it saturate or dead-band at the edges?
Is the 40 mm look-ahead enough to control the sharpest bend, or does the robot lag and leave the line on tight curves?
Is 12 mm footprint resolution sufficient, or do 8 mm or 16 mm sensors give a cleaner signal?
Does steering_oscillation indicate geometry-driven jitter, for example from sensor spacing or wheel track, rather than controller tuning?

intent: Baseline symmetric five-sensor array, 12 mm footprints at 15 mm pitch, placed 40 mm ahead of the axle for look-ahead. Mid-range wheel track and radius, moderate mass. Purpose: establish a reference platform and measure how sensor resolution, look-ahead and track width affect completion, line loss and rms error. Next iteration I will adjust based on the Integrator's feedback on signal quality and steering authority.
learning: No prior iterations. Baseline chosen from the public contract ranges. Revisit sensor pitch, look-ahead distance and wheel track after the first race telemetry.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or integration feedback yet, so this is a neutral baseline meant to give the Integrator a clean platform to tune. Five sensors spread across the 25 mm tape at 15 mm pitch (x = -0.030 to +0.030 m) with 12 mm footprints. Adjacent footprints overlap the tape edge, so the reading stays informative for a line offset of up to about ±0.03 m, and the outer sensors can see a sharp bend early. The sensors sit 0.04 m ahead of the axle, which gives roughly 0.04 m of look-ahead on a 1.5 m/s run, enough to react before the robot is off-line. Track width 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn authority without excessive yaw inertia. Body 0.16 m x 0.12 m is well inside the off-track limit, and mass 0.8 kg keeps acceleration reasonable for a 3 s finish. Expected result: a completing run on the development tracks with few line losses. The main unknown is whether 12 mm sensors at 15 mm pitch give enough resolution, which the Integrator's feedback should show.
